stem.en: When a net force acts on an object, the object accelerates:

text.en: opposite to the force, with acceleration proportional to the force.

feedback.en: The acceleration is in the direction of the net force, not opposite to it.

text.en: opposite to the force, with acceleration proportional to the mass.

feedback.en: The acceleration is along the net force, and a larger mass gets a smaller acceleration.

text.en: along the force, with acceleration inversely proportional to the force.

feedback.en: A larger force gives a larger acceleration, not a smaller one.

text.en: along the force, with acceleration proportional to the force.

feedback.en: Right. This is what the second law says.

explanation.en: Newton's second law: the object accelerates in the direction of the net force, and a = F / m. So the acceleration is proportional to the force.

hints.en: Recall a = F / m. Which way does the acceleration point?
